item.title: Third China-US Track 1.5 Dialogue held in Beijing focuses on political trust, trade and AI cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25 12:33:00
Photo: VCG The third China-US Track 1.5 Dialogue was held in Beijing on Tuesday, bringing together representatives from Chinese government departments, local governments and think tanks, as well as US representatives from organizations including the Asia Society, CCTV News reported. Participants will hold discussions on how to enhance political mutual trust, expand economic and trade cooperation, and explore cooperation in artificial intelligence, science and technology. Established in 2023, the dialogue operates between formal government-to-government diplomacy, known as Track 1, and purely nongovernmental exchanges, known as Track 2. The dialogue has become an important platform for communication among political parties, strategic communities, business communities, academic institutions and civil society in both China and the US. Previous meetings have produced a range of concrete proposals for strengthening bilateral exchanges and cooperation in political, economic, trade, technological and people-to-people fields, according to CCTV News. item.title: Largest-diameter underwater tunnel in the world operational in China, passing beneath Yellow River: report
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25 11:47:00
The world’s largest-diameter underwater shield tunnel has been completed and officially put into operation in Jinan city, East China’s Shandong Province on August 25, 2026. Photo: Xinhua News Agency The world’s largest-diameter underwater shield tunnel has been completed and officially put into operation in Jinan city, East China’s Shandong Province, Xinhua News Agency reported on Tuesday. The tunnel has a total length of about 5,755 meters, featuring a single-bore, double-deck design with a designed speed of 60 kilometers per hour. The shield section stretches about 3,290 meters and was constructed using a tunnel boring machine (TBM) with an excavation diameter of 17.5 meters. The tunnel is the first single-bore, double-deck shield tunnel in China to pass beneath the Yellow River, with the construction route crossing sensitive areas including the Yellow River embankment and the river itself. The project overcame 28 major technical challenges, including excavation stability control, settlement control when passing beneath the Yellow River embankment, uplift control of large-section tunnel segments, and green, efficient treatment of massive amounts of slurry. It achieved a maximum daily excavation rate of 18 meters and a monthly advance rate of 426 meters, setting a world record for 17-meter-class shield tunneling. In recent years, China’s shield tunneling industry has seen continued market expansion, significant improvements in technological capabilities and accelerating global expansion. As a core piece of equipment for underground engineering, shield machines have entered a growth phase driven by both domestic demand and exports, Chinese experts said. Technological advances are enabling rapid breakthroughs in engineering projects, while China’s tunnel boring machine industry is moving from large-scale application toward higher levels of intelligence, efficiency and global competitiveness. Global Times

item.title: US' cancellation of marine drills with South Korea highlights declining US security commitment to allies: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25 11:45:00
The Ssangyong major amphibious assault drills held by the South Korean and the US Navy and Marine Corps in September, 2024. Photo: VCG After scaling down the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises with South Korea, the US has reportedly canceled a large-scale joint amphibious landing exercise with South Korean forces scheduled for September, with Seoul citing resource constraints linked to the US-Israeli war in Iran. Beyond the Iran war-related force constraints, Chinese experts said the cancellation could also be aimed at supporting US President Donald Trump’s intention to resume direct diplomacy with North Korea. The move, nonetheless, highlights declining US security commitment to its allies, a military expert noted. “The US Marine Corps formally notified our forces in June that its ability to deploy forces during this year’s Ssangyong exercise would be constrained due to the situation in the Middle East,” a spokesperson for the South Korean marine corps told reporters, according to Reuters. Ssangyong, or “Twin Dragons,” is a biennial exercise that involves US and South Korean marines rehearsing amphibious landings with the use of warships, aircraft and ground forces. It has taken place for decades and involves more than 10,000 marines from both countries, according to media reports. While Ssangyong was previously shelved during Trump’s first term — when he dismissed major exercises as “provocative” and too expensive amid his personal diplomacy with the North Korean leader — it was revived in 2023, according to the New York Times. This cancellation follows Trump’s surprise announcement last week to cut back a separate joint military drill with South Korea known as Ulchi Freedom Shield. The exercise, which began August 17 and ended Friday, was slashed from 11 days to five over what Trump claimed was a desire to resume diplomatic talks with North Korea and Seoul’s refusal to help the US in the Iran war. The main reason for canceling Ssangyong may not be the war in Iran, but rather Trump’s intention to send a goodwill signal to Pyongyang and pave the way for the resumption of direct diplomacy, Chinese military affairs expert Song Zhongping told the Global Times. However, Song noted that it remains to be seen whether such a move would elicit a similar gesture of goodwill from North Korea, saying that Pyongyang would expect sincere and substantive steps from the US on issues concerning its core interests rather than gestures. Kim Yo Jong, department director of the Central Committee of the Workers' Party of North Korea, said on August 19 that “as for the reduction of the US-ROK joint military drill abruptly announced by the US president a few days ago, we regard it as the one unworthy of comment and have no interest in it at all. The reduction of the scale and duration of the drill does not mean the change of the nature of the military drill with a provocative and offensive feature,” according to the official Korean Central News Agency. Asked about the “substantially reduced” joint military exercises between the US and South Korea and whether China supports renewed dialogue between the US and the DPRK at a regular press briefing on August 17, Lin Jian, a spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry, said that “we noticed relevant reports. A peaceful and stable Peninsula and a political settlement of the Korean Peninsula issue are in the interest of all parties.” Meanwhile, the US’ approach could further strain Washington’s relations with its allies. One trend is becoming increasingly clear: the era in which the US was willing to shoulder a substantial share of the security burden for its allies is fading; on that broader shift, US Republicans and Democrats have increasingly moved in the same direction, Song noted.

item.title: 2026 APEC SME ministerial meeting to focus on innovation, cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25 08:46:00
A themed installation is pictured at a business district in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Aug. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) The 32nd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Ministerial Meeting will be held on Sept. 4 in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) said on Monday. The meeting, themed "innovation-driven development for win-win cooperation," will bring together SME officials from APEC economies, representatives of the APEC Secretariat, and other guests. The meeting will focus on technological innovation, digital empowerment and inclusive development, with a joint ministerial statement and other outcome documents expected, according to Liang Zhifeng, director of the SME bureau under the MIIT. As the host, China hopes that through in-depth exchanges, all economies will reach forward-looking and practical consensus, promote mutual learning of policies and the translation of outcomes, and jointly enhance the innovation capacity, digitalization level and sustainable development capabilities of SMEs in the Asia-Pacific region, said Vice Minister of Industry and Information Technology Ke Jixin. Wang Sheng, vice governor of Guangdong, said that all preparations for the meeting are essentially complete, and all APEC economies had confirmed their participation. More than 2,100 companies from home and abroad have registered for the accompanying exhibitions, with over 3,900 booths planned. China will host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in south China in November this year, which will mark the country's third hosting of the event following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. This year marks the APEC "China Year," with the theme of "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together." Approximately 300 APEC-related meetings and events will take place in multiple Chinese cities throughout the year.

item.title: Nvidia wants to 'copy China's homework' and we welcome it: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25 01:09:00
Nvidia Photo: VCG While the US is still debating whether "openness is safe," China is building an open, low-cost and decentralized AI ecosystem around the world. This openness reflects a deeper understanding of the very nature of technology. In this sense, if Nvidia treats open source merely as a marketing tool for generating chip orders rather than genuinely committing to building an open, collaborative ecosystem, then the "American DeepSeek" may well turn out to be nothing more than an expensive shell. Several US media outlets recently reported that Nvidia is spending $6 billion to build one of the world's most powerful open-weight AI models, in a bid to compete with Chinese heavyweight models such as DeepSeek and Kimi K3. One of the key contexts behind this move is that most US AI giants have poured far more resources into closed AI models, while the tremendous success of China's open-source models has sparked significant anxiety within the US, making "whether to pivot to open source" a heated topic of debate in the industry. Therefore, Nvidia's turn toward open-weight models has attracted attention. Admittedly, Nvidia's primary motivation is to enter the open-source arena in the face of intense competition, support startups, and thereby secure more chip orders. But objectively speaking, the move is also a sign that the myth of closed-source AI in the US is being further shattered. Previously, the US AI industry was dominated by closed models, with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google controlling the closed-source ecosystem. Before the emergence of China's DeepSeek, the market firmly believed that closed source AI is the future. When Chinese open-source models burst onto the scene with low cost, customizability, and local deployability, developers and businesses worldwide suddenly woke up to just how significant the drawbacks of the closed-source models really are. Thus, Nvidia's $6 billion bet on open-source models has led some media to dub it an attempt to build an "American DeepSeek." Notably, the debate over open versus closed source within the US is evolving from a dispute over technical approaches into a contest over strategic direction. Some US political elites and security bureaucrats still cling to the Cold War mentality that "control means security," trying to lock AI technology within their own camp through export controls and investment screening. OpenAI and Anthropic are lobbying vigorously in Washington, urging restrictions on Chinese open-source models and hyping the false narrative of "distillation" - essentially using national security as an excuse to mask their commercial monopoly interests. Because once open-source models match or even surpass closed-source models in performance, their subscription models and application programming interface businesses on which they depend on will face a fundamental challenge. However, faced with China's open-source approach and its increasingly strong capacity for independent innovation, a growing number of people in the US technology industry are realizing that the containment strategy will not only fail to curb the growth of China's open-source ecosystem, but will also cause the US to lose its own competitive edge. Not long ago, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang took the rare step of spearheading an open letter on the social media platform in support of open source, prompting Microsoft, Google, Meta and other major players in the industry to publicly voice their support. Several US tech companies have also established the Open Secure AI Alliance (OSAA), which reportedly now has more than 230 members. All of this reflects a broader shift in thinking across the US tech industry. In a sense, Nvidia's $6 billion bet on open source is essentially adding fuel to the open-source movement in the US tech industry. From the attention sparked by DeepSeek to the debut of flagship models such as GLM-5.2 and Kimi K3, the global open-source AI ecosystem, driven largely by Chinese companies, has demonstrated the resilience of this approach and the strength of its development capabilities. In the long run, a thriving open-source community depends on broad participation, transparent mechanisms for collaboration and low barriers to access - not monopolistic investment by any single tech giant. For Nvidia, therefore, whether this money is well spent will depend on chip sales in the short term, model performance in the medium term, and, in the long term, whether it can truly understand the logic of open source. If Nvidia treats open source merely as a marketing tool for generating chip orders rather than genuinely committing to building an open, collaborative ecosystem, then the "American DeepSeek" may well turn out to be nothing more than an expensive shell. Even so, we welcome Nvidia "copying the homework." The value of AI technology lies in making it widely accessible, not keeping it locked away. While the US is still debating whether "openness is safe," China is building an open, low-cost and decentralized AI ecosystem around the world. This openness reflects a deeper understanding of the very nature of technology. Today, open-source models have attracted an ever-growing number of developers worldwide, while countries across the globe are developing their own large language models based on open-source technologies from China. China has demonstrated through concrete actions that openness does not weaken competitiveness; on the contrary, it can give technology greater vitality. As more and more countries choose to join the open ecosystem, the "small yard, high fence" approach will ultimately be swept away by the tide of the times. The ultimate significance of AI lies in enabling every individual and every country to share equally in the benefits of technological progress. From this perspective, open source is not merely a technological approach, but also a choice of values. In the race of open source, the judges are not a handful of Silicon Valley giants, but are the choices of countless developers and users around the world. Nvidia's decision to "copy China's homework" is certainly worth watching, but what matters even more is that a growing number of participants are proving through their actions that openness is the future of AI.

item.title: GT Voice: For the prospects of robotics, industry vitality speaks louder than skepticism
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24 22:36:00
Visitors watch a robot folding clothes at the 2026 World Robot Conference in Beijing, August 19, 2026. Photo: VCG As Chinese-made humanoid robots are making spectacular performance at the 2nd World Humanoid Robot Games (WHRG), the commercial prospects of humanoid robots have become a topic of discussion among some Western media outlets. The Economist published an article on Sunday headlined "China will struggle to make money from humanoid robots," which focuses on development challenges such as the high data collection costs facing the sector, casting doubt on the commercial viability of the emerging industry. This perspective does capture the bottlenecks the industry faces in data acquisition and the efficiency of model training. But to judge the commercialization prospects of an emerging industry, one cannot fixate on cost alone. The sustainability of an emerging sector hinges not on temporary bottlenecks, but on the maturity of its industrial ecosystem, richness of application scenarios, and continuous evolution of business models. Take Unitree Robotics, a leading Chinese humanoid robot company, as an example. Unitree's revenue rose to about 1.7 billion yuan ($253 million) in 2025 from 159 million yuan in 2023, with its net profit reaching 288 million yuan in 2025, according to thepaper.cn. More importantly, Unitree's revenue structure has undergone an important change. In 2025, humanoid robots overtook quadruped robots to become Unitree's highest‑revenue product line for the first time. According to its prospectus, the company's humanoid robot revenue reached approximately 877 million yuan in 2025, accounting for more than half of its main business revenue, while actual shipments for the full year exceeded 5,500 units. Profitability at one leading firm does not indicate full industry maturity, but it at least proves the commercial value of humanoid robots within China's robust supply chain and high-quality manufacturing ecosystem. The current skepticism surrounding humanoid robots closely mirrors the doubts that plagued industrial robots in their early days. Yet the global industrial robot industry eventually achieved dramatic cost reductions through large scale adoption in real world scenarios. The commercial path for humanoid robots is not a simple replica of industrial robots. Humanoid robots rely heavily on artificial intelligence (AI) large-language models and require vast amounts of real‑world data or high‑quality simulated training datasets. Their cost structure encompasses not only hardware but also software. Yet, because they are built on an AI foundation, once the core bottlenecks are overcome, their scenario adaptability, application value, and ultimate industrial ceiling will far exceed that of traditional industrial robots. Whether China's robotics industry can achieve commercial viability does not hinge on a single company's financial results, but on the vitality and innovation of the industrial ecosystem. China has more than 1.165 million entities related to the robotics industrial chain, with approximately 144,000 newly added since the beginning of this year. Moreover, the new entrants in the robotics industry are no longer limited to complete machine manufacturers. They are increasingly focused on algorithm development, system integration, scenario specific solutions, software platforms, and engineering services. The trend of integration among robotics and AI, software, and automation systems is becoming more pronounced. Collectively, these developments, spanning manufacturing infrastructure, diverse application demands, technological breakthroughs, and engineering capabilities, have propelled the rapid growth of China's humanoid robot industry and given the country a comprehensive comparative advantage in mass manufacturing and product supply. This systemic advantage is already translating into real-world results. While most global markets are still exploring the possibilities of technology and cost, Chinese companies have already delivered tens of thousands of units in real world scenarios, continuously optimizing performance and cost structures through intense market competition. Data released by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology in July showed that more than 400 complete humanoid robot products had been developed in China, accounting for more than half of the global total. According to a report released at the Second WHRG, China shipped more than 40,000 humanoid robots in the first half of 2026, accounting for 97 percent of global shipments. This scale of deployment itself has laid a solid foundation for the commercialization of humanoid robots. While the global market is watching whether humanoid robots can overcome the profitability barrier, China's surging industrial advance is itself the most direct answer.

item.title: Sanae Takaichi must understand the true meaning of 'a state cannot stand once it has lost the confidence of the people': Hai Feng
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24 19:25:00
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi responds to questions from party leaders regarding PM Takaichi's policy speech during the House of Councillors plenary session at the Diet building in Tokyo on February 25, 2026. Photo: VCG According to a Japanese media report on August 21, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi recently posted a series of lengthy messages on social media to defend herself against mounting criticism, even quoting the phrase "a state cannot stand once it has lost the confidence of the people" from The Analects of Confucius in a desperate bid to rally public support. Japanese political commentators noted that these moves reflect her sense of urgency. Nevertheless, Japanese public opinion is not buying her rhetoric, given her practice of saying one thing but doing another. In her posts, Takaichi claimed that she was mentally prepared for "a certain degree" of criticism, adding, "But 'a state cannot stand once it has lost the confidence of the people' - without the trust of the public, a government cannot stand." She also noted that if she cannot gain the public's trust as prime minister, it may hinder the implementation of future policies. Takaichi invoked The Analects of Confucius in an attempt to "limit the damage," but the problem is that she treats this quote merely as a public relations ploy without truly understanding its deeper meaning. "A state cannot stand once it has lost the confidence of the people" is not a shield to be wielded while simultaneously betraying that trust and demanding the public's tolerance. Confucius' maxim was never intended to teach people how to "justify" a breach of trust, but rather how to "prevent" it; it does not address how those in power should defend themselves in the public sphere, but rather what they must do to earn the people's trust. The dictum "a state cannot stand once it has lost the confidence of the people" comes from The Analects of Confucius: Yan Yuan. When Zi Gong asked about the way to govern a country, Confucius replied: "Sufficient food, sufficient military preparedness and the trust of the people." Abundant grain supplies, capable national defense and public confidence were the three cornerstones of sound governance. Zi Gong pressed further, asking what should be abandoned first if, out of necessity, one had to give up one of these in turn. Confucius answered "drop military might," and then "drop food supplies." This left the timeless maxim: "Death has always been with us, but a state cannot stand once it has lost the confidence of the people." Confucius could not have made the order of priority among food, military strength and trust in the governance of state any clearer; of these three, public trust is the most important. Without military preparedness, a nation faces instability; without food, the people suffer hardship; but once the trust of the people is lost, the government cannot even stand. This is because food ensures survival, military preparedness guarantees security, but only trust sustains the most fundamental political relationship between the state and its people. Therefore, Takaichi's problem today is not merely "why her approval ratings are falling," but rather "why the people no longer trust her." The reasons are not hard to fathom. First, a failure to address people's livelihoods. Surging prices and rising living costs represent the most tangible and immediate source of anxiety in Japanese society. Ordinary people care about their wallets, their incomes and grocery bills - not the countless lengthy posts and explanations churned out on social‑media platforms. With real‑life hardships all too evident, hollow excuses can hardly win over public trust. Second, a failure of self‑reflection. Faced with a continuous decline in approval ratings, if a leader is unwilling to even acknowledge where the problem lies - or worse, adopts an attitude of "I don't know the reason" or "I have nothing to reflect on" - that is not merely a lack of understanding of public sentiment, but a lack of respect for it. The greatest fear in politics is not making mistakes, but making mistakes without realizing it, and clinging to appearances even after losing the people's trust. Third, moral failings in dealing with history. A political figure who truly understands that "a state cannot stand once it has lost the confidence of the people" would never repeatedly test the limits on historical issues, much less continuously send the wrong signals on major topics such as the history of aggression, the shadow of militarism, and regional peace and security. As soon as Takaichi took office, she made erroneous remarks regarding Taiwan and has been racing down the dangerous and misguided path of reviving militarism. Being dishonest about history, wavering in her commitment to peace and lacking basic respect for neighboring countries - this "breach of trust" is by no means merely a diplomatic misstep; ultimately, it will also erode her domestic political credibility. Ultimately, Takaichi's problem is that she pays lip service to "trust" while her actions undermine it; she quotes The Analects of Confucius but her conduct runs counter to The Analects of Confucius' principles of governance. She sees only the result - a decline in her approval ratings - but refuses to acknowledge that the cause lies in her own gradual erosion of trust. Ancient Chinese political wisdom has long offered a more profound explanation of this. The Book of History states: "The people are the foundation of a state, and the state will have peace when the foundation is solid." The Words of Mencius goes a step further, asserting: "The people are the most important; the nation is the next; the sovereign is least." In other words, power is not meant to demand understanding from the people. It exists to respond to them, serve them and hold them in reverence. This is the true essence of the saying "a state cannot stand once it has lost the confidence of the people." Trust is not a written statement, a citation of classical texts, a string of lengthy posts on social media, or a cultural prop resorted to at the last minute when a crisis strikes. Trust stems from the ruler's integrity, sincerity, sense of responsibility and willingness to correct mistakes and reflect. It comes from keeping the people's hardships close to one's heart and arises from upholding moral boundaries on matters of principle. If Takaichi truly wishes to understand The Analects of Confucius, she should not merely use the phrase "a state cannot stand once it has lost the confidence of the people" to gloss over her own shortcomings. She should first ask herself: Why has she betrayed the trust of her own citizens? Why has she betrayed the trust of neighboring countries? Why has she betrayed the trust of historical justice? This quote from Confucius is by no means an excuse to exonerate her. On the contrary, it serves as a clear mirror that lays bare the true intentions of those in power.

item.title: China's cyberspace regulator intensifies crackdown on group livestream misconduct
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24 13:44:00
Photo of group livestream. Photo: VCG China's cyberspace regulator has shut down more than 7,200 illegal group livestreaming rooms and penalized over 2,200 accounts as part of an intensified crackdown on misconduct in online group livestreaming entertainment. The campaign targets vulgar content, mechanisms designed to encourage excessive tipping, and infringements on minors' rights. The Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) has also instructed online platforms to remove or take action against a number of MCN agencies involved in serious misconduct, issued 17 notices on the campaign, and publicized typical cases to deter further violations, said regulator on its WeChat account. During a campaign, the CAC has sought to combine enforcement with tighter regulation by improving content review, adjusting ranking systems and interactive features, and strengthening oversight of group livestreaming accounts and MCN agencies. Online platforms have also been urged to assume greater responsibility for managing such content. Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok, has begun displaying information about affiliated MCN agencies on group livestreaming accounts and has organized training for agencies to curb misconduct at the source. Kuaishou, one of China's popular short-video platforms, has refined its review standards and strengthened technical tools to better identify vulgar content and inappropriate interactions. WeChat Channels have introduced an identity-verification mechanism for suspected underage participants in group livestreams with the aim to preventing minors from appearing in such broadcasts in disguised or less obvious ways. Bilibili, a Chinese video platform, meanwhile, has removed features such as multiplier points, tiered bonuses and ranking competitions that could encourage viewers to spend money on virtual gifts. Xiaohongshu, or RedNote, Chinese equivalent of Instagram, has imposed measures including traffic restrictions to curb practices such as repetitive shouting and livestreaming competitions that lack substantive content. The CAC said that the campaign has led to a significant decline in vulgar content in entertainment group livestreaming, while violations involving the inducement of excessive tipping have been effectively curbed. The regulator said it will maintain strict oversight, intensify action against accounts and agencies that violate regulations, and push online platforms to improve management mechanisms and technological capabilities. It will also continue to optimize livestreaming features to foster a healthier and more orderly online entertainment environment. Global Times

item.title: Two Chinese sailors rescued, 22 missing after Panama-flagged bulk carrier sinks off eastern India's coast; operation still ongoing: embassy tells GT
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24 10:16:00
Caption: The Indian Coast Guard and the Indian Navy have launched a joint rescue operation after the Panama-flagged bulk carrier Ocean Winner sank in waters off the coast of Paradip, India's Odisha state. Photo: Screenshot of NDTV's report Two Chinese sailors have been rescued after a Panama-flagged bulk carrier carrying 24 crew members sank in the Bay of Bengal, about 230 nautical miles off the coast of Paradip, India's Odisha state, as Indian authorities intensified search-and-rescue operations for the remaining 22 crew members, according to multiple Indian media outlets and Reuters. The two sailors were rescued from life rafts by MT Aisopos, a commercial vessel operating nearby, after an Indian Navy P-8I maritime surveillance aircraft located the rafts during the search-and-rescue mission, the Times of India reported. The Chinese embassy in India told the Global Times that the rescue operation is still ongoing. The two Chinese seafarers said the vessel, called Ocean Winner, had developed a list on Friday and sank within eight minutes, forcing the crew to abandon ship, Reuters reported, citing Shyam Jagannathan, director general of India's Maritime Administration. Jagannathan said the chances of finding survivors generally fall sharply after the first 12 hours, but rescuers were continuing their search. "All agencies are coordinating closely and actively doing search and rescue efforts," Sarbananda Sonowal, federal minister for India's Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, said in a social media post, according to Reuters. India has experience and capabilities in maritime rescue operations in the Indian Ocean, and the practice is part of the country's international humanitarian responsibilities. Yet its active efforts to rescue the Chinese crew members could still leave a positive impression among Chinese people and allow the public to feel India's goodwill, which may improve China-India relations, Lin Minwang, deputy director of the Center for South Asian Studies at Fudan University, told the Global Times on Monday. Having relevant officials continue to follow up on the rescue efforts and convey goodwill could further demonstrate India's willingness to improve ties with China, Lin said. Ocean Winner, with IMO number 9145530, was a 70,000-deadweight-ton bulk carrier built in 1998. It loaded iron ore at Paradip and departed for Singapore on Thursday with 24 crew members aboard, according to Maritime Executive. The vessel's Automatic Identification System signal disappeared in the middle of the Bay of Bengal at 4:45 pm GMT on Friday. The crew issued a distress alert at around the same time, the report said. India has long sought the role of a security provider in the Indian Ocean and a major regional power. When maritime emergencies occur in the region, the Indian Navy and Coast Guard are capable of providing relatively timely assistance, Lin added. The 22 missing crew members include 18 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi, according to the Indian Coast Guard. Two Coast Guard vessels were dispatched from Sri Vijaya Puram, formerly known as Port Blair and the capital of India's Andaman and Nicobar Islands, to join the search-and-rescue operation, according to a Coast Guard spokesperson cited by Reuters. Separately, Maritime Executive noted that iron ore fines can become hazardous when wet, as the cargo may liquefy and suddenly shift to one side while a vessel is rolling. This induces a list, accompanied by free surface effect, with serious adverse impact on stability. From 2007 to 2019, 29 seafarers were killed in casualties involving iron ore cargoes, the outlet reported.
